maya: heads up from staging run — after switching kernel-selector -> fast-path-v2, host preparse + tokenizer CPU spiked for tiny requests (~<64 tokens).

jamal: which pool? rtx? gtx?

maya: rtx-pool only so far. gtx-pool didn't show it.

ken: any quick flame output?

maya: pasted perf sample (top lines):
```
  preparse_loop    48%   kernel_fast_v2::coalesce_and_tokenize
  frame_unpack     19%   proto_unmarshal
  writev_syscall   12%   net::small_writes
```

sofia: fast-path-v2 enabled the adaptive-mini-batcher, right? that does extra CPU to gather fragments.

maya: yes. hypothesis: tokenizer normalizes prefixes, batcher merges fragments and preparse normalizes again (safety path) -> duplicate work.

jamal: interesting. also saw increased kvcache evictions during the window. could the batcher change the fragment keying pattern?

maya: good catch. brief stats from 60s window:
```
before: avg_seq=36, p95=62, kvmiss=2.7%
after:  avg_seq=35, p95=63, kvmiss=9.8%
```

maya: miss spike aligns with deploy window. suspect composite frames create many short-lived keys.

ken: can we add a metadata bit from tokenizer that marks frames as "canonical-normalized" so preparse can skip? cheap header flag.

sofia: that would avoid duplicate normalize. need to verify across private clusters where old tokenizers might not send flag. backward compatible check required.

ingress-bot: deploys/staging/fast-path-v2 complete  1733509600 by maya

maya: plan proposal (short-term):
- add 1-bit header "NORM=1" from tokenizer to indicate normalized
- disable adaptive-mini-batch for requests <=64 tokens as a canary
- bump kvcache shard limit on rtx-pool by +8% (ops approval needed)

jamal: for medium-term, maybe change cache keying: use request-root-hash + fragment-index instead of hashing entire composite payload. reduces fragmentation. but streaming resume semantics might be tricky.

ken: try the header bit first. also capture GRPC vs HTTP traces — I think http2 coalescing produces more small writev calls; grpc path seems noisier.

maya: captured syscall diffs: writev count (per-second): pre=120/s, post=310/s on grpc path. http1 path increase was much smaller.

sofia: that explains tail latency: more syscalls -> higher kernel overhead for tiny fragments. we could adjust http2 frame coalesce threshold for small requests.

jamal: I'll run a kvcache micro-sim with the new keying scheme and post numbers. want to see hit-rate delta under identical request mix.

maya: quick perf regression numbers I recorded:
- median E2E small request latency: pre=40ms, post=52ms
- p95: pre=110ms, post=190ms
- host preparse CPU: pre=16%, post=39%
- allocator tail events (tokenizer): +3.6x

ken: rough rollout idea: ship header bit + disable minibatch for <=64 tokens as immediate mitigations. if that doesn't land us back to baseline within 12-24h, roll back fast-path-v2.

sofia: agree. header-bit PR should include unit + integration test to ensure we never skip normalize for untrusted frames. I'll draft PR template.

maya: implementing header-bit now. adding a safety flag: if header present but origin != tokenizer-service, we still run normalize. safe fallback.

jamal: sim queued. will post hit-rate + eviction curves in this thread when done (~3h).

ken: also attach flamegraphs and perf IDs here for the incident log. keep the rollback window short. :thumbsup:

maya: uploaded flamegraph -> perf-id fg-173350-01. will drop link when artifact finishes.

sofia: thx everyone. please tag this thread when PRs are open so we can track.

maya: will update after canary runs (~2h).
